profiles.name: Apollo A6000
profiles.summary: ApolloOS (AROS based) boots from the bundled 128 GB CompactFlash card. Two full-size SD slots are used for data exchange and, per the A6000 manual, as an alternate RDB boot device.

interfaces.name: SD slot - data exchange card (FAT32)

facts.text: Apollo supports SDHC microSD/SD cards for data exchange.
If ApolloOS can already read the card, Apollo advises not to reformat it.
If the card is not readable, format it FAT32 with Rufus: non-bootable, volume label SD0, quick format, no extended label files.
ApolloOS is not compatible with every factory FAT32 format; reformatting with the Rufus recipe is the documented fix.
Mount the card from the ApolloOS Start Menu: SD Card > Mount.
Tested: a card prepared by this app (MBR, FAT32, label SD0) mounts as SD0 and files can be read and written.

unverified: Behaviour with SDXC cards larger than 32 GB (Apollo lists SDHC). FAT32 is still created, but a warning is shown.
Whether ApolloOS reads a FAT32 card that has no MBR (superfloppy layout).

interfaces.name: SD slot - Amiga hard drive card (RDB)

facts.text: The A6000 manual describes one SD slot as removable storage or an alternate boot device using a native (RDB) bootable OS image.
Partitions that have not been formatted appear as 'Uninitialized' after they are mounted and must be formatted.
ApolloROM only boots ApolloOS; Kickstart ROMs only boot AmigaOS.

unverified: Which physical slot (left or right) accepts the RDB boot card - sources disagree.
Whether ApolloOS auto-mounts RDB partitions from the SD slot or requires SDMount / a mountlist.
Whether ApolloOS ships a PFS3 or SFS handler, or the handler must be embedded in the RDB.
Largest FFS partition ApolloOS handles reliably on sagasd.device (4 GiB is used as a conservative cap).
Correct MaxTransfer for sagasd.device (0x1FE00 is used as the conservative classic value).

interfaces.name: CompactFlash (IDE) - ApolloOS system drive

facts.text: The A6000 ships with a 128 GB CompactFlash card with ApolloOS preinstalled.
ApolloOS distribution images are written to the card with an image writer such as Win32DiskImager.
The A6000 boots ApolloOS from the CompactFlash card.

unverified: The partition layout of the shipped ApolloOS CompactFlash image. This app never repartitions this card; it only backs it up or restores an authorised image.

profiles.name: Amiga 1200
profiles.summary: Internal 44-pin Gayle IDE with an SD or CF adapter, partitioned with an RDB exactly like a real Amiga hard drive (as HDToolBox does).

interfaces.name: Internal IDE (SD/CF-to-IDE adapter)

compatibilityModes.name: Kickstart 3.0 / 3.1 (ROM scsi.device, FFS 40)
notes: The ROM scsi.device cannot address beyond 4 GB; every partition must end below that point.
FFS 40 partitions are kept at or below 2 GB, the common safe limit.

compatibilityModes.name: Kickstart 3.1 + TD64/NSD-capable scsi.device and filesystem
notes: Requires a patched scsi.device (e.g. from AmigaOS 3.9 / 3.1.4) and a TD64/NSD aware filesystem such as PFS3AIO or FFS 45+ loaded before mounting large partitions.
The boot partition should still end below 4 GB.

compatibilityModes.name: Kickstart 3.1.4 / 3.2
notes: The 3.1.4/3.2 ROM scsi.device and FFS support large disks. Long filenames (DOS\7) require 3.2.

facts.text: The RDSK block must be within the first 16 blocks of the disk.
FFS boot block holds the DosType; the root block is at the middle of the partition.

unverified: Not yet tested on real A1200 hardware; layouts are validated with amitools (rdbtool/xdftool).

interfaces.name: PCMCIA slot - CF/SD adapter (FAT32 data card)
unverified: Needs a PCMCIA card driver (e.g. compactflash.device) and a FAT filesystem handler (e.g. fat95, or CrossDOS on AmigaOS 3.1.4/3.2) installed on the Amiga.
Which card sizes and FAT32 cluster sizes the installed handler accepts; 32 GB or smaller is assumed to be safest.
Many SD-to-PCMCIA adapters are unreliable on the A600/A1200 PCMCIA port; this has not been tested.

profiles.name: PiStorm (Emu68)
profiles.summary: PiStorm accelerator running Emu68 on a Raspberry Pi: the SD card holds a FAT32 boot partition for Emu68 and an Amiga partition (type 0x76) with its own RDB.

interfaces.name: Raspberry Pi SD card (Emu68)

compatibilityModes.name: Kickstart 3.1.4 / 3.2
notes: Large partitions are fine with the 3.1.4/3.2 FFS.

compatibilityModes.name: Kickstart 3.1 (FFS 40)
notes: FFS 40 partitions are kept at or below 2 GB.

facts.text: Emu68 boots from the contents of its install directory copied onto a FAT32 or FAT16 formatted SD card.
Amiga partitions on the card use MBR partition type 0x76; under AmigaOS they are reached through the brcm-sdhc.device (Pi 3/Zero 2) or brcm-emmc.device (Pi 4/CM4).

unverified: That each 0x76 partition is presented by Emu68 as its own unit containing a standard RDB (this tool writes one RDB inside the 0x76 partition).
Boot partition size: 256 MB is created; Emu68 itself needs far less.
The Emu68 files (from an Emu68 release) and a Kickstart ROM are not included: copy them onto the EMU68 boot partition with Windows Explorer after preparing.
Not tested on PiStorm hardware; structures are validated with amitools.
